# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles WGS84 coordinates, occupational spans and benchmark population series for 146 excavated settlement, marshland and valley complexes (437 benchmark observations, averaging 2,99 per settlement, with 116 spanning at least three benchmarks) across Great Basin Hydrological Unit 16 from 7500BC to 1600AD [@kelly2025; @bird2022p3k14c]. The inventory links 76 Bonneville-Wasatch Fremont and Shoshone sites (Provo River Timpanogos Capital, Backhoe Village, Five Finger Ridge, Nephi Mounds, Pharo Village, Ogden River Confluence Metropolis, Logan River Shoshone Capital, Parowan Gap-Paragonah, Median Village, Nawthis Village, Baker Village, Evans Mound), 46 Humboldt-Lahontan wetland and Sierra-margin complexes (Lovelock Big Meadow Capital, Fallon Carson Sink Capital, Carson City Eagle Valley Capital, Wadsworth Truckee Bend Capital, Yerington Mason Capital, Stillwater Marsh, Pyramid Lake Paiute Village, Walker Lake Paiute Village, Lake Tahoe (Tahoe Reach), Bridgeport Valley Village, Martis Valley, Falcon Hill) and 24 Central Nevada-Owens-Mojave valley centres (Fish Lake Valley Capital, Pahrump Spring Oasis Capital, Belmont Toquima Range Capital, Caliente Meadow Valley Capital, Eureka Diamond Valley Capital, Gatecliff Shelter) [@meighan1956paragonah; @kelly2001marsh; @lawton1976owens; @jennings1957danger]. Source-ledger reconciliation confirms 146 included settlements and 180 excluded entries (162 duplicate-alias consolidations and 18 unquantified non-habitation cave and rockshelter exclusions) across all 326 evaluated candidates with zero unaccounted entries.

# Background

Durable Great Basin habitations clustered where perennial mountain streams intersected alluvial fans or productive lacustrine marshes. Along the eastern Great Basin rim, Fremont farmers constructed adobe granaries and semi-subterranean pithouse villages at Provo River Timpanogos Capital (1,15k), Backhoe Village (1,06k at 1000AD), Five Finger Ridge (1,06k at 900AD), Nephi Mounds (1,06k at 1150AD), Pharo Village (1,06k at 975AD), Parowan Gap-Paragonah (828 at 900AD), Median Village (583 at 700AD) and Nawthis Village (480 at 1100AD) [@meighan1956paragonah; @finley2020fremont].

In the Lahontan Basin of western Nevada, long-duration marsh adaptations at Lovelock Big Meadow Capital (1,2k), Fallon Carson Sink Capital (1,15k), Carson City Eagle Valley Capital (1,02k) and Stillwater Marsh (480) anchored semi-sedentary cattail, bulrush and tui chub harvesting from the late Archaic to contact, joined by lakeshore Paiute settlements at Pyramid Lake Paiute Village (320), Walker Lake Paiute Village (240), Lake Tahoe (Tahoe Reach) (190) and Bridgeport Valley Village (135) on the southern Sierra margin [@kelly2001marsh; @lawton1976owens; @bettinger1982numic]. Early lakeside shelters and open camps including Falcon Hill (7500BC to 1500BC, 35 peak), Grimes Point (5000BC to 800AD, 60 peak), Amy's Shelter (3500BC, 25 peak) and Gatecliff Shelter (3500BC, 35 peak) preserve foraging baselines back to the Early Holocene, complemented by non-habitation stratigraphic caves such as Danger Cave and Hogup Cave [@jennings1957danger].

# Methodology

## Gazetteer Compilation and Exclusion Rules

Candidates were screened under CENTAUR gazetteer criteria requiring documented WGS84 coordinates, dated residential horizons and quantified village, marsh-cluster or habitation headcounts [@bird2022p3k14c; @kelly2025]. Across 326 evaluated candidates in the regional source ledger, 162 duplicate-coordinate twins consolidated into canonical entries and 18 non-habitation caves and rockshelters lacking permanent residential structures (Danger Cave, Hogup Cave, Lovelock Cave, Spirit Cave, Bonneville Estates Rockshelter and Promontory Cave 1) are excluded, leaving 146 included settlements [@jennings1957danger]. All benchmark years follow GMT+0.

## Village and Wetland-Cluster Estimation

Fremont village figures derive from excavated pithouse and surface-granary counts scaled by phase contemporaneity and regional architectural tiers [@meighan1956paragonah; @finley2020fremont]. Wetland-complex and Paiute-Shoshone estimates for Lovelock Big Meadow Capital, Fallon Carson Sink Capital, Stillwater Marsh, Pyramid Lake Paiute Village and Bridgeport Valley Village aggregate contemporaneous residential house-pit clusters and ethnohistorically documented irrigated or marsh territories [@kelly2001marsh; @lawton1976owens].

# Testing and Validation

Ledger checks confirm exact correspondence between the 146 included settlements in the settlement gazetteer and the 326 candidates in the regional source ledger, alongside 180 excluded entries (162 duplicate-alias consolidations and 18 unquantified non-habitation caves; Table \ref{tab:coverage-sett-great-basin}). Seventy-six sites sit in the Bonneville-Wasatch Oasis (52,1%), 46 in the Humboldt-Lahontan Corridor (31,5%) and 24 in Central Nevada-Owens-Mojave (16,4%). Chronological checks reproduce the eastern-western structural contrast: most Utah Fremont villages peak between 900AD and 1250AD and terminate by 1300AD, whereas Lahontan and Numic wetland villages (Stillwater Marsh, Pyramid Lake Paiute Village, Walker Lake Paiute Village, Bridgeport Valley Village) sustain or expand populations through 1500AD to 1550AD (with Stillwater Marsh continuing to 1600AD) [@kelly2001marsh; @lawton1976owens].

```{r tab-coverage, results='asis'}
reg_list <- mod_json$regions
s_reg <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) as.character(e$region_id), character(1))
s_obs <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) length(e$population), integer(1))
s_pk <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) max(unlist(e$population)), numeric(1))
s_nm <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) as.character(e$name), character(1))
cov_rows <- lapply(names(reg_list), function (rk) {
  idx <- which(s_reg == rk)
  best <- idx[which.max(s_pk[idx])]
  data.frame(
    Subregion = gsub("&", "and", sub("^\\d+\\.\\s*", "", reg_list[[rk]]$name), fixed = TRUE),
    Sites = viscount_fmt_number(length(idx), 0L),
    Share = paste0(viscount_fmt_number(100 * length(idx) / length(sett_json), 1L), "%"),
    Obs = viscount_fmt_number(sum(s_obs[idx]), 0L),
    TopSite = paste0(s_nm[best], " (", viscount_fmt_pop(s_pk[best]), ")"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_cov <- do.call(rbind, cov_rows)
rownames(df_cov) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_cov,
  "Sub-regional distribution of the 146 catalogued settlements and benchmark observations across Great Basin HU 16.",
  c("Sub-Region", "Sites", "Share", "Obs.", "Leading Site (Peak)"),
  list(label = "tab:coverage-sett-great-basin", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Results

## Leading Settlement Gazetteer

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-great-basin} presents the Top 45 settlements ranked by peak population descending out of the 146 catalogued sites across HU 16, and Figure \ref{fig:settlements-great-basin} plots the rank-size hierarchy led by Lovelock Big Meadow Capital (1,2k), Fallon Carson Sink Capital (1,15k), Provo River Timpanogos Capital (1,15k), Backhoe Village, Five Finger Ridge, Nephi Mounds and Pharo Village (1,06k each), Ogden River Confluence Metropolis (1,05k) and Carson City Eagle Valley Capital (1,02k).

```{r tab-gazetteer, results='asis'}
fmt_cell_pop <- function (p) {
  if (is.null(p) || is.na(p)) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}
fmt_yr_era <- function (y) {
  if (y < 0L) paste0(abs(y), "BC") else paste0(y, "AD")
}
pk_vec <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) max(unlist(e$population)), numeric(1))
nm_vec <- vapply(sett_json, function (e) as.character(e$name), character(1))
ord_idx <- order(-pk_vec, nm_vec)
top_setts <- sett_json[ord_idx[seq_len(min(45L, length(ord_idx)))]]
rows <- lapply(top_setts, function (e) {
  yrs <- sort(as.integer(names(e$population)))
  pk <- max(unlist(e$population))
  span_str <- paste0(fmt_yr_era(min(yrs)), "-", fmt_yr_era(max(yrs)))
  coord_str <- paste0(viscount_fmt_number(e$coords[[1]], 2L), ", ", viscount_fmt_number(e$coords[[2]], 2L))
  data.frame(
    Settlement = e$name,
    State = e$country,
    Coords = coord_str,
    Span = span_str,
    Peak = viscount_fmt_pop(pk),
    Y0 = fmt_cell_pop(e$population[["0"]]),
    Y800 = fmt_cell_pop(e$population[["800"]]),
    Y1100 = fmt_cell_pop(e$population[["1100"]]),
    Y1500 = fmt_cell_pop(e$population[["1500"]]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_gaz <- do.call(rbind, rows)
rownames(df_gaz) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_gaz,
  "Top 45 Fremont, wetland marsh and desert settlements in Great Basin HU 16 ranked by peak population.",
  c("Settlement", "State", "Coords (Lat, Lon)", "Span", "Peak", "0AD", "800AD", "1100AD", "1500AD"),
  list(label = "tab:gazetteer-great-basin", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

```{r fig-settlements, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig4_great_basin_settlements.png",
  "Rank-size distribution and leading fifteen settlement hierarchy across the 146 catalogued complexes in Great Basin HU 16.",
  "fig:settlements-great-basin"
)
```

## Source Ledger Audit

Table \ref{tab:ledger-great-basin} documents the leading 30 of 180 excluded candidate records (162 duplicate-alias consolidations and 18 non-habitation cave exclusions) from the 326 evaluated entries in the regional source ledger.

```{r tab-ledger, results='asis'}
exc_cands <- Filter(function (cnd) !identical(cnd$status, "included"), ledger_json$candidates)
if (length(exc_cands) > 30L) exc_cands <- exc_cands[seq_len(30L)]
l_rows <- lapply(exc_cands, function (cnd) {
  data.frame(
    Candidate = gsub("&", "and", as.character(cnd$name), fixed = TRUE),
    State = cnd$country,
    Status = cnd$status,
    Reason = gsub("_", " ", cnd$reason),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_led <- do.call(rbind, l_rows)
rownames(df_led) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_led,
  "Leading thirty excluded candidate records (out of 180 total exclusions) from the 326 evaluated entries in Great Basin HU 16.",
  c("Candidate", "Jurisdiction", "Status", "Ledger Classification"),
  list(label = "tab:ledger-great-basin", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Limitations

Three limitations affect site-level resolution in HU 16. First, Lovelock Big Meadow Capital, Fallon Carson Sink Capital and Stillwater Marsh represent multi-locus wetland catchment clusters rather than compact walled towns, meaning reported totals aggregate contemporaneous marsh-rim camps [@kelly2001marsh]. Second, Central Nevada Valleys, Owens Valley and Mojave Endorheic Basin holds 24 catalogued settlements led by Fish Lake Valley Capital (790) and Pahrump Spring Oasis Capital (760), while dispersed Shoshone and Paiute seasonal camps across Owens Valley left ephemeral brush architecture captured chiefly in sub-regional carrying capacities [@bettinger1982numic; @lawton1976owens]. Third, the four leading Sevier-Parowan Fremont villages (Backhoe Village, Five Finger Ridge, Nephi Mounds, Pharo Village) share a 1.060-person standardised regional architectural tier ceiling, flattening fine-grained site differences near the upper end of the rank-size curve (Figure \ref{fig:settlements-great-basin}).
